rows.question: linear search algorithm ka main goal kya hota hai?

rows.answer:
Linear search ka main goal kisi array mein ek specific element (jise 'key' kehte hain) ko dhundhna hota hai. Isme hum array ke pehle element se shuru karke har element ko sequentially check karte hain jab tak ya toh key mil na jaaye, ya poora array khatam na ho jaaye.

Agar key mil jaati hai, toh hum uska index return karte hain, aur agar nahi milti, toh hum -1 return karte hain.

rows.question: linked list aur array mein kya difference hota hai?
rows.gold_answer: The lecture only discusses arrays and does not provide a comparison with linked lists.
rows.question_hi: linked list aur array mein kya difference hota hai?
rows.question_en: What is the difference between a linked list and an array?
rows.answer:
The lecture you're currently watching focuses specifically on searching within arrays, so it doesn't cover the differences between arrays and linked lists.

In general, the main difference is how they store data: an array stores elements in contiguous (side-by-side) memory locations, which allows for fast, direct access to any index. A linked list, on the other hand, stores elements in nodes scattered in memory, where each node points to the next one, making it more flexible for inserting or deleting elements but slower for accessing a specific index.

rows.question: linear search ka time complexity O(log n) kyun hota hai?
rows.gold_answer: The time complexity of linear search is actually O(n), not O(log n), because it requires traversing the entire array.
rows.quote: Kyunki n size ka agar array hai, toh hum poore array ko traverse kar rahe hain, toh uski jo time complexity ho jaayegi, woh ho jaayegi O(n).
rows.question_hi: linear search ka time complexity O(log n) kyun hota hai?
rows.question_en: Why is the time complexity of linear search O(log n)?
rows.answer:
Actually, linear search ka time complexity $O(\log n)$ nahi, balki $O(n)$ hota hai.

Linear search mein hum array ke har element ko ek-ek karke check karte hain, isliye agar array ka size $n$ hai, toh worst-case mein humein $n$ baar operations karne padte hain. $O(\log n)$ complexity binary search ki hoti hai, jahan hum har step mein search area ko aadha (half) kar dete hain.
